images.title: Same border, three shapes
images.purpose: Show three rectangles with a border of 20 units, 5 by 5, 7 by 3 and 9 by 1, so that the one closest to a square visibly holds the most squares.
images.composition: Three rectangles stacked, each with its border outlined and its perimeter and area written on the right.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. At the top, centred at x 728 and y 62, the heading Same border, three shapes in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (44 px). Three rectangles stand one above the other, all with a border of 20 units, with the unit square 36 by 36 px: (1) a rectangle of 5 by 5 unit squares, 180 by 180 px, at x 100 to 280 and y 100 to 280, filled amber #E69F00 with thin dark #2B2B2B grid lines (2 px) and a thick teal #0072B2 outline (6 px) round its whole border; to its right, at x 760, the three lines of text 5 by 5, Perimeter 20 units and Area 25 square units, centred vertically on the rectangle (36 px, dark #1F2937); (2) a rectangle of 7 by 3 unit squares, 252 by 108 px, at x 100 to 352 and y 330 to 438, filled amber #E69F00 with thin dark #2B2B2B grid lines (2 px) and a thick teal #0072B2 outline (6 px) round its whole border; to its right, at x 760, the three lines of text 7 by 3, Perimeter 20 units and Area 21 square units, centred vertically on the rectangle (36 px, dark #1F2937); (3) a rectangle of 9 by 1 unit squares, 324 by 36 px, at x 100 to 424 and y 490 to 526, filled amber #E69F00 with thin dark #2B2B2B grid lines (2 px) and a thick teal #0072B2 outline (6 px) round its whole border; to its right, at x 760, the three lines of text 9 by 1, Perimeter 20 units and Area 9 square units, centred vertically on the rectangle (36 px, dark #1F2937). In all 3 rectangles. No other number and no other text anywhere. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a rectangle whose border is not 20 units, or rectangles drawn with different unit squares
a perimeter or area value other than the ones listed
images.takeaway: Shapes with the same perimeter can have different areas: 25, 21 and 9 square units for a border of 20 units.
images.description: Three rectangles with a perimeter of 20 units: 5 by 5, 7 by 3 and 9 by 1, with areas 25, 21 and 9 square units.
images.context: Concept image for Same Perimeter, Different Area. It follows the idea of the shapes of Let Us Explore in your maths book and uses the numbers of this concept's own example.
images.teaching_notes: Let the student see that the 9 by 1 strip has the same border as the square but holds far fewer squares. The slip to watch: believing a bigger perimeter must hold more squares.

image_decisions.why: The three outlined rectangles put 'same border, different area' in one look.
